lessons.title: Lesson 1: How drone law is built
lessons.text:
Lesson 1 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Find and name the layers of drone law that apply in your country.
This lesson builds toward: For your own country, you will find the civil aviation authority's drone regulations, standards and fee schedule and name each layer of drone law, with links and the date you checked.
Countries base their aviation rules on international standards from ICAO, the UN's International Civil Aviation Organization, but each country writes and enforces its own drone law. Usually there is an aviation act passed by parliament; drone regulations made under that act; implementing standards or manuals with the technical detail; a fee schedule; and notices or circulars for special cases.
Most modern drone rules sort operations by risk. Low-risk flying (small drone, in sight, low, away from people and airports) has the lightest requirements. Higher-risk flying (heavy drones, beyond sight, over people, near aerodromes, spraying or dropping things) needs more: authorisation, certified operators, licensed pilots, and sometimes certified aircraft.
To find your country's rules, go to the civil aviation authority's website and look for a section called drones, UAS, RPAS or unmanned aircraft. Download the regulations, the standards and the fee schedule, and note the date. Examples of authorities: KCAA (Kenya), NCAA (Nigeria), and the civil aviation authorities of Ghana, Rwanda, Uganda, Tanzania and South Africa.
Step by step:
- Open your civil aviation authority's website.
- Find the drones / UAS / RPAS section.
- Download the regulations, implementing standards and fee schedule.
- Note the date and version of each.
- List how the rules sort operations by risk.
Words to know:
- ICAO: the International Civil Aviation Organization, a UN agency that sets international aviation standards.
- Regulations: legally binding rules made under an act of parliament.
- Implementing standards: detailed technical rules that explain how to meet the regulations.
- Risk category: a group of operations with similar risk and similar requirements.
Official sources:
- Kenya Civil Aviation Authority (KCAA): Unmanned Aircraft Systems
- Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA): Nig.CARs 2023 Part 21, Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems
Try it now: For your country, list the aviation authority, the name and year of the drone regulations, whether there are implementing standards and a fee schedule, and the date you checked. Save the documents in one folder.
You can now find the layers of drone law in your country and see how they sort operations by risk.

check.q: What is a fee schedule in drone law?
options: A list of the approvals that exist and what each costs
check.why: The fee schedule lists the approvals and their charges, so it shows what exists.

check.q: You want your country's drone rules. Where do you look first?
options: The civil aviation authority's website, in its drones, UAS or RPAS section
check.why: Each country's civil aviation authority publishes its own drone regulations, standards and fees.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Kenya: KCAA and the UAS Regulations 2020
lessons.text:
Lesson 2 of 6 · about 6 minutes
Goal: List the Kenyan approvals a commercial agricultural drone operator is likely to need.
This lesson builds toward: Given a commercial agricultural drone job in Kenya, you will list the KCAA registrations, licences, certificates and authorisations it is likely to need, naming the regulations they come from and that current fees and new rules must be checked.
In Kenya, drones are governed by the Civil Aviation (Unmanned Aircraft Systems) Regulations, 2020, made under the Civil Aviation Act, 2013, and overseen by KCAA. KCAA's drone page also publishes a Manual of Implementing Standards and a fee schedule, the Civil Aviation (Regulatory Fees and Charges for Unmanned Aircraft Systems) Regulations, 2020.
The fee schedule shows the main approvals that exist: an import permit and registration for the drone; certificates of airworthiness; a Remote Air Operator Certificate (ROC) for operators; operation authorisations for Category A and for Categories B and C; licences for people, including a student remote pilot licence, a remote pilot licence (RPL), and ratings such as beyond visual line of sight; and approvals for training organisations and for drone resellers. KCAA lists approved ROC holders and training organisations on its site, and applications go through its online drone system.
KCAA's site also lists newly published Kenya Civil Aviation Regulations for 2026. Check whether any of them change the drone rules before relying on the 2020 versions, and check current fees on the day you apply.
Words to know:
- KCAA: Kenya Civil Aviation Authority, which regulates drones in Kenya.
- ROC: Remote Air Operator Certificate: KCAA's approval for an organisation to run drone operations.
- SRPL / RPL: student remote pilot licence / remote pilot licence.
- Certificate of airworthiness: an official confirmation that an aircraft is fit and safe to fly.
Official sources:
- Kenya Civil Aviation Authority (KCAA): Unmanned Aircraft Systems
- Kenya Law: The Civil Aviation (Unmanned Aircraft Systems) Regulations, 2020 (L.N. 42 of 2020)
- KCAA: Civil Aviation (Regulatory Fees and Charges for Unmanned Aircraft Systems) Regulations, 2020 (L.N. 4 of 2021)
- KCAA: Remote Air Operator Certificate (ROC)
- KCAA: Unmanned Aircraft Systems Training Organizations (UTO)
- KCAA drone (RPAS) online system
- KCAA: Kenya Civil Aviation Regulations 2026 (published regulations)
Try it now: Open KCAA's drone page and fee schedule. Make a table of every approval a business mapping tea estates for pay would need (drone, people, organisation, operation), with a column for where to apply. Leave fees as "check on the day".
You can now list the Kenyan registrations, licences, certificates and authorisations a commercial farm-drone operator is likely to need, and where to apply.

check.q: What is an RPL in Kenya?
options: A remote pilot licence for the person who flies
check.why: The remote pilot licence (RPL) is the licence for the person who flies.

check.q: You plan to apply to KCAA next month using the 2020 rules. What do you check first?
options: Whether KCAA's newly published regulations change the drone rules, and the current fees
check.why: KCAA lists newly published regulations, and fees must be checked on the day you apply.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Nigeria: NCAA and Nig.CARs Part 21
lessons.text:
Lesson 3 of 6 · about 6 minutes
Goal: Classify a drone and operation under Nigeria's Part 21 and list what it requires.
This lesson builds toward: Given a drone's weight and a planned operation in Nigeria, you will classify the drone and the operation's risk category under Part 21 and list the operating limits that apply, with the right weight class and risk category.
In Nigeria, drones are covered by Part 21 (Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems) of the Nigeria Civil Aviation Regulations 2023, document Nig.CARs/2023/021, effective 17 May 2023, overseen by the NCAA. It covers certification, registration, operations and surveillance of RPAS.
Part 21 classifies aircraft by weight: Nano (under 250 g), Micro (250 g to under 2 kg), Small (2 kg to under 25 kg), Medium (25 kg to 150 kg) and Large (over 150 kg), each with conditions and prior authorisation from the Authority. It also uses three operational risk categories: Open (lowest risk, must be registered), Specific (higher risk, needs authorisation) and Certified (aircraft, operator and pilot certified, treated more like manned aviation). It provides for remote pilot licences and RPAS operator certificates.
Part 21 also sets operating limits, for example flights at or below 120 m (400 ft) above ground in many cases, keeping 30 m horizontally from people not involved in the operation, not flying over populated areas, and staying away from aerodromes (such as within 4 km of a controlled aerodrome's movement area, or 10 km for private and recreational flights) unless authorised. Read the full text for the conditions that apply to your operation.
Words to know:
- NCAA: Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority, which regulates drones in Nigeria.
- Nig.CARs: Nigeria Civil Aviation Regulations.
- Open / Specific / Certified: Part 21's three operational risk categories, from lowest to highest risk.
- Movement area: the part of an airport used by aircraft to take off, land and taxi.
Official sources:
- Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA): Nig.CARs 2023 Part 21, Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems
Try it now: A Nigerian agribusiness wants to map cassava farms in Ogun State with a 1.2 kg multirotor and a 15 kg multirotor for spraying. Using Part 21, write each drone's weight class, the likely risk category of each job, and three questions you would ask the NCAA.
You can now classify a drone and an operation under Nigeria's Part 21 and list what it requires.

check.q: Under Part 21, which category needs the aircraft, operator and pilot to be certified?
check.why: The Certified category is treated more like manned aviation, with certified aircraft, operator and pilot.

check.q: A farmer in Nigeria asks you to fly 10 m from people at a village market who are not part of the job. What do you do?
options: Keep at least 30 m away from uninvolved people and avoid populated areas unless authorised
Ask the people to look away
check.why: Part 21 keeps many operations 30 m from uninvolved people and away from populated areas.

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Pilot licences and operator certificates
lessons.text:
Lesson 4 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Plan the people and organisation approvals for a drone service business.
This lesson builds toward: For a drone service business, you will plan the pilot licences and the operator certificate it needs and the documents the operator certificate asks for, separating approvals for the person who flies from approvals for the business.
Two kinds of approval matter for a business. The person who flies needs the pilot licence and any ratings the rules require; in Kenya, the remote pilot licence (RPL), trained at a KCAA-approved training organisation; in Nigeria, a remote pilot licence under Part 21. The organisation that sells drone services usually needs an operator certificate: KCAA's Remote Air Operator Certificate or NCAA's RPAS Operator Certificate.
Operator certification usually asks for evidence that the business can operate safely: an operations manual (how you plan, fly, maintain and report), named responsible people, trained and licensed pilots, registered drones, a maintenance system, records, and insurance. Part 21, for example, lists third-party liability insurance certificates among the documents an operation must carry.
Plan time and money for this. Ask the authority for its current checklist and fees, and ask approved training organisations whether they help with operations manuals.
Step by step:
- List every pilot and the licence and ratings each needs.
- Check the operator certificate your business needs.
- Get the authority's current application checklist.
- Draft an operations manual: planning, flying, maintenance, emergencies, reporting.
- Arrange insurance and record systems.
Words to know:
- Operations manual: a business's written rules for how it plans, flies, maintains drones and handles emergencies.
- Third-party liability insurance: insurance that pays if your operation harms other people or their property.
Official sources:
- KCAA: Remote Air Operator Certificate (ROC)
- KCAA: Unmanned Aircraft Systems Training Organizations (UTO)
- Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA): Nig.CARs 2023 Part 21, Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems
Try it now: Write the table of contents for an operations manual for a small crop-mapping business, with at least eight sections (for example: organisation, responsibilities, flight planning, pre-flight checks, emergencies, maintenance, records, incident reporting).
You can now plan the pilot licences and operator certificate a drone service business needs, and what an operations manual covers.

options: A licence for the person who flies
An approval for the organisation that sells drone services
check.why: The operator certificate, such as KCAA's ROC or NCAA's RPAS Operator Certificate, is for the business.

check.q: You are preparing to apply for an operator certificate. Which document do you write first?
options: An operations manual for planning, flying, maintenance and reporting
check.why: Operator certification usually asks for an operations manual showing how the business operates safely.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Special operations: spraying, BVLOS and aerodromes
lessons.text:
Lesson 5 of 6 · about 6 minutes
Goal: Identify operations that need extra approvals and who gives them.
This lesson builds toward: Given a job that involves spraying, BVLOS, night flying or an aerodrome, you will identify the extra aviation and pesticide approvals it needs and who gives them, before offering or planning the job.
Spraying pesticides or dropping anything from a drone is a special operation. Part 21, for example, forbids dropping or discharging things in a way that creates a hazard and has separate rules for dangerous goods, and Kenya's fee schedule lists separate authorisations for higher-risk categories. Many pesticides are classed as dangerous goods. Expect to need specific aviation authorisation, a heavier certified aircraft, and trained crews.
Spraying also falls under pesticide law. In Kenya, pest control products are regulated by the Pest Control Products Board (PCPB); in Nigeria, agrochemicals are regulated by NAFDAC. Ask them whether the product may be applied from the air and what training and protective equipment applicators need. FAO and WHO have published guidance for aerial application of pesticides. Never spray, or offer spraying, without both aviation and pesticide approvals.
Other special operations include flying beyond visual line of sight (BVLOS), at night, near or at aerodromes, over people or roads, and in restricted or protected areas such as national parks. Each needs specific approval. Large farms near airstrips are common in Africa: check distances and ask before planning.
Words to know:
- Dangerous goods: materials that can harm health, safety or property in transport, such as many pesticides.
- Pesticide regulator: the government body that registers pesticides and controls how they are used.
- BVLOS: beyond visual line of sight.
Official sources:
- Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA): Nig.CARs 2023 Part 21, Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems
- KCAA: Civil Aviation (Regulatory Fees and Charges for Unmanned Aircraft Systems) Regulations, 2020 (L.N. 4 of 2021)
- Pest Control Products Board (Kenya)
- National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC, Nigeria)
- FAO and WHO: Guidance for aerial application of pesticides (2024)
Try it now: A sugarcane estate 3 km from an airstrip asks you to spray a fungicide by drone. List every approval and check you would need (aviation, pesticide, landowner, aerodrome) and who you would contact for each.
You can now spot special operations and list the aviation and pesticide approvals they need.

check.q: Which body regulates agrochemicals in Nigeria?
check.why: In Nigeria, agrochemicals are regulated by NAFDAC; aviation approvals come from NCAA.

check.q: An estate asks you to spray fungicide by drone next week. You have a pilot licence only. What do you do?
options: Do not offer spraying until you have both the aviation and pesticide approvals
Spray early in the morning when nobody is around
Use a lighter drone and spray anyway
check.why: Spraying needs specific aviation authorisation and pesticide approvals; never spray without both.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Building and keeping a compliance file
lessons.text:
Lesson 6 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Build a compliance file and a schedule to keep it current.
This lesson builds toward: For your drone business, you will build a compliance file and a schedule for renewals and rule checks, with every required document listed and its status.
A compliance file holds everything that proves your operation is legal and safe, in one place you can show an inspector, a client or an insurer. Keep a paper copy and a backed-up digital copy.
Include: the regulations and standards you follow (with dates checked); registration certificates for each drone; import permits; pilot licences and ratings; the operator certificate; operation authorisations; the operations manual; insurance certificates; maintenance records; flight logs; incident reports; client agreements and landowner permissions; and your data protection steps (Kenya: ODPC; Nigeria: NDPC) if you hold farmers' personal data.
Rules, fees and forms change. Keep a renewal calendar for every licence and certificate, and check the authority's website on a fixed schedule, for example monthly, and before every new type of job. Write down what you checked and when.
Step by step:
- Create the file: paper and backed-up digital.
- Add regulations, certificates, licences, authorisations, manual, insurance.
- Add maintenance records, flight logs, incident reports, agreements.
- Add data protection registration or steps if you hold personal data.
- Set a renewal calendar and a monthly rules check.
Words to know:
- Compliance: following the laws and rules that apply to you.
- Renewal: applying again before a licence or certificate expires.
Official sources:
- Kenya Civil Aviation Authority (KCAA): Unmanned Aircraft Systems
- KCAA: Kenya Civil Aviation Regulations 2026 (published regulations)
- Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA): Nig.CARs 2023 Part 21, Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems
- Office of the Data Protection Commissioner (Kenya)
- Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC)
Try it now: Final task: build the compliance file for a drone service business in your country: authority and regulations with dates, classification and risk category, every approval and its status, required documents, extra spraying approvals if planned, data protection steps, and a renewal and rules-check calendar.
You can now build and maintain a compliance file that shows your drone operation is legal and safe.
How your final task is checked:
What we look at Not yet Meets Exceeds Authority and regulations The authority or regulations are missing, or there are no links or dates. The authority, regulations, standards and fee schedule are listed with links and the date checked. Also notes any newly published rules and how they change the job. Classification and risk The drone's class or the operation's risk category is missing or wrong. The drone's classification and the operation's risk category are correct for the country's rules. Lists the operating limits, such as height and distance from people, that apply. Approvals needed Approvals are missing, or who issues them is not named. Every registration, permit, licence, certificate and authorisation is listed with who issues it and its status. Includes current fees and a timeline for getting each one. People and business documents The operations manual, insurance or records are missing. Pilot licences, operator certificate, operations manual, insurance, maintenance and flight records are listed. Names the responsible people and where each document is kept. Spraying and special operations Spraying or other special operations are planned without extra approvals. The extra aviation and pesticide approvals for any special operation are listed with who gives them. Explains how aerodrome distances and dangerous goods rules affect the job. Keeping it current No renewal dates or rule-check schedule; no data protection steps. A renewal calendar, a fixed schedule for rule checks, and data protection steps for farmers' data. Has a log showing past checks and what changed. To pass: Meets or Exceeds on every row. If a row is Not yet, fix that part of the file and check it again.

check.q: What belongs in a compliance file?
options: Licences, certificates, authorisations, the operations manual, insurance and records
check.why: A compliance file holds everything that proves your operation is legal and safe.

check.q: Your remote pilot licence expires in three months. What keeps you from missing it?
options: Waiting for KCAA to call you
A renewal calendar with every licence and certificate date
Checking only when a client asks
Keeping the licence in the drone case
check.why: A renewal calendar and fixed checks keep every licence and certificate current.
